newsitem.title: USA: Union cites Fedex workers' raise as organizing win.
newsitem.headline: Union cites Fedex workers' raise as organizing win.

text.p: The Teamsters union claimed a partial victory Friday in its drive to organize Federal Express Corp. workers by taking credit for a 3 percent raise it said the company promised hourly employees.

The union said company Chief Executive Fred Smith reversed himself on Thursday by announcing that workers would receive the raise in April, after telling employees several months ago that the Memphis-based express delivery service would substitute regular raises with a "pay performance" system.
"FedEx workers have already won a big victory as a result of their Teamster organizing," International Brotherhood of Teamsters General President Ron Carey said in a statement.

But FedEx sharply disputed the union's claims, saying that it has had a performance-based compensation system in place for several years and denying that employees were told there would be an across-the-board 3 percent raise.

"What they say we did is not true," said company spokesman Greg Rossiter. He said Smith addressed employees recently as he does every quarter. Although regular salary and compensation adjustments were discussed, he said it had nothing to do with the union's organizing effort.
"They are trying to claim credit for something that we do every quarter," said Rossiter. "They're claiming credit for something that has nothing to do with them."
He declined to elaborate on FedEx's various pay programs. FedEx has 110,000 employees in the United States, most of them hourly, he said.
The union, which is based in Washington, said the "pay performance" system required employees to attain goals that they considered nearly impossible to achieve.

The Teamsters said Smith also reversed himself on another matter, first telling workers that their profit-sharing yields would be distributed in their retirement accounts and Thursday giving them an option to take a lump sum cash payment instead.
The union said it has signed up thousands of workers and that workers in eight FedEx locations already have petitioned for elections with the National Labor Relations Board.
Congress, however, has affirmed that FedEx is covered under the Railway Labor Act, which is administered by the National Mediation Board, not the NLRB.
